name: Chatbase
tagline: The credit-metered AI chatbot builder that turns a website crawl into a customer-facing support agent in minutes.
tldr: Chatbase is a no-code platform for building custom AI chatbots trained on your own content (website crawls, documents, Q&A) and embedding them on your site, WhatsApp, or other channels.

Pricing is metered in monthly message credits rather than seats or conversations — 50 credits free, 700 on Hobby ($40/mo, or $32/mo billed annually), 4,000 on Standard ($150/mo, or $120/mo annually), 15,000 on Pro ($500/mo, or $400/mo annually), with heavier models consuming more credits per reply.
Higher tiers unlock voice, telephony, helpdesk features, outbound campaigns, API access, and CRM/helpdesk integrations like Stripe and Zendesk — the Free and Hobby tiers are website-widget-only.
Bootstrapped and founder-led by solo founder Yasser Elsaid (no outside investors), reportedly crossing roughly $9M ARR with a lean ~30-person Toronto-based team as of 2026.

Independent reviews are split: strong marks for ease of setup and fast time-to-launch, but recurring complaints about billing/credit costs, occasional hallucinated answers, and slower support responses.
keyFeatures: Train an agent on crawled website pages, uploaded documents, plain text, or Q&A pairs, with auto-retraining on Standard tier and above
Message-credit billing model where model choice affects cost (e.g. premium models consume more credits per response than standard models)
Voice and telephony support plus a helpdesk/ticketing layer on the Standard plan and up
Native integrations with tools like Stripe, Zendesk, and other business systems on higher tiers
Outbound campaign tooling for proactive messaging, in addition to reactive support replies
API access for embedding chatbot logic into custom applications
Enterprise tier with SSO, white-labeling, audit logs, HIPAA-eligible configuration, and zero data retention options
Analytics dashboards that get more advanced (ticket sourcing, deeper reporting) at the Pro tier

faq.question: How does Chatbase pricing actually work?
faq.answer: Plans are priced monthly and include a pool of message credits rather than a flat conversation cap: Free (50 credits), Hobby $40/mo (700 credits), Standard $150/mo (4,000 credits), Pro $500/mo (15,000 credits) — each drops about 20% ($32/$120/$400) if billed annually. Using a premium model like a top-tier Claude or GPT model can burn multiple credits per single reply, so real usage costs vary with model choice.

faq.question: Can Chatbase read live product prices or stock from my store?
faq.answer: Chatbase trains primarily on crawled/uploaded static content, so live data like stock levels needs to be kept current through re-crawls or connected via integrations/API rather than assumed to update automatically.

faq.question: Does Chatbase support channels beyond the website widget?
faq.answer: Yes — voice and telephony are available starting on the Standard plan, and the platform supports WhatsApp and API-based custom integrations, though the free and Hobby tiers are effectively website-widget-only.

faq.question: Is Chatbase good for enterprise/compliance-heavy teams?
faq.answer: The Enterprise tier adds SSO, audit logs, white-labeling, and a HIPAA-eligible, zero-data-retention configuration, but pricing is custom and requires contacting sales.

faq.question: What do users complain about most?
faq.answer: The most consistent criticisms are around cost scaling with credit consumption, occasional hallucinated answers outside the trained knowledge base, and reports of slower customer support response times on certain plans.

scorecard.note: Reviewers consistently cite fast time-to-launch — crawl a site, tune the prompt, embed a widget, no code required.
Capable for FAQ-style answers but multiple reviews report hallucinations outside the trained knowledge base, and quality depends heavily on which model tier you're paying for.
Solid on web widget and API; voice/telephony and WhatsApp exist but are gated behind Standard tier and above.
Credit-based billing makes costs unpredictable at scale, and add-ons (extra agents, branding removal, auto-recharge) stack up quickly on top of the sticker price.
Support quality trails ease-of-use on third-party review aggregates, and multiple reviewers report slow or unhelpful support interactions.

criteriaScores.note: Official docs confirm dedicated integrations for website widget, email, WhatsApp, Facebook Messenger, Instagram DM, and voice (Twilio/SIP phone calls), plus Slack; the Twilio doc explicitly covers inbound phone calls only, with no native SMS integration found.

Chatbase's Helpdesk overview docs describe a single dashboard managing tickets from website, email, WhatsApp, Messenger, Instagram, and API in one place, with filtering by channel, assignee, and status rather than separate per-channel inboxes.
Chatbase is a genuine RAG-based AI agent trained on crawled/uploaded content with tool-calling 'Actions' (API calls, Shopify/Stripe lookups, ticket creation) rather than canned/scripted replies.

No independently verified resolution-rate figure is published by Chatbase. Capterra and G2 reviews repeatedly describe the bot generating confidently wrong answers ('the bot WILL generate a totally wrong answer with that greatest of eloquence and confidence' — Capterra review), so this is scored conservatively based on independent sentiment rather than any vendor claim.

Docs confirm automatic weekly re-crawling/auto-retrain for connected website, Notion, and remote-storage (Google Drive/Dropbox) sources, plus a manual 'Retrain agent' option — no manual intent-building required.

Chatbase supports prompt-based restriction to trained sources and confidence-based handoff to a human/lead form when uncertain, but citation behavior is not rigorous by default (URLs must be explicitly present in training content to be cited reliably), and independent reviews still report frequent hallucinated answers outside the knowledge base.

The 'Actions' system supports multi-step agentic workflows beyond if/then rules: ticket escalation, live-agent handoff (Chatbase/Salesforce/Sunshine), Stripe billing actions, Shopify order/product actions, and custom API-calling actions with client-side code execution.
The Analytics dashboard has a dedicated Sentiment section that automatically detects user sentiment/emotion per conversation, plus an automatic Topics section for intent categorization.
The Helpdesk consolidates tickets from website chat, email, WhatsApp, Messenger, Instagram, and API into one dashboard with per-customer conversation history, filterable by channel/assignee/status.

Docs describe one-click live takeover ('AI pauses on click. Toggle the AI back on immediately when the human is done') within the same conversation thread, plus dedicated escalation Actions to Chatbase, Salesforce, and Sunshine live chat.
The Helpdesk message composer has a separate internal-only 'Note' tab, and tickets support auto-assignment to teams/agents via routing rules; no documented @mention feature was found.

A dedicated Shopify Action lets the agent 'recommend products, answer order questions, and provide delivery updates' with real order tracking; refund processing and live inventory access are not documented.

Chatbase's own blog copy claims WooCommerce support ('Chatbase integrates with Shopify, WooCommerce, Magento, and any custom store'), but unlike Shopify there is no dedicated WooCommerce integration doc page or Action — no evidence of order/refund lookups specific to WooCommerce.
Chatbase has a dedicated WordPress plugin in the official plugin directory (install, activate, enter Agent ID) in addition to the universal embed script that works as a widget on any site.
A dedicated Wix setup guide exists in Chatbase's docs for embedding the widget on Wix sites.

No dedicated Chatbase-Squarespace integration page was found (a direct docs URL for it 404s), unlike Wix, WordPress, and Webflow which each have first-party guides; third-party sources only surface Zapier/Albato workarounds.
A dedicated Webflow doc page walks through embedding the agent via Webflow's embed code feature with display customization.

Zapier is a documented native integration (draft/categorize email responses, push AI-generated ticket solutions into Jira/Intercom/Zendesk, capture leads); no native Make.com or n8n integration was found in Chatbase's own docs.

HubSpot and Salesforce both have dedicated integration docs, but both are escalation/ticketing-focused (HubSpot: create tickets; Salesforce: respond to/escalate cases) rather than full contact/deal data sync — no Pipedrive integration was found.

The Shopify Action provides real order-question and delivery-update lookups, and a separate Stripe Action lets the agent 'handle billing, invoices, and subscription queries in chat' — genuine data access, though refund execution isn't documented.
Chatbase supports 80+ languages with automatic detection for conversations, and a changelog entry confirms the chat widget UI itself localizes to match the visitor's browser language.

The Analytics tab confirms Chats, Topics, and Sentiment sections with date filtering, and Pro tier adds 'advanced analytics' and ticket-sourcing reporting; explicit CSAT surveys, first-contact-resolution, or per-agent performance scorecards were not found in the documentation.

Plan prices and credit pools are clearly published, but real cost per conversation is unpredictable since credit consumption varies 1-5x by model choice, and several add-ons (extra agents $25/mo each, auto-recharge $40 per 1,000 credits, remove-branding $99/mo) stack on top of the sticker price.

Chatbase offers a REST API v2, webhook events (leads.submit, {action}_collect_data.submit) with HMAC-SHA1 signature verification, and custom Actions that call arbitrary external APIs or run client-side code — real extensibility beyond the vendor's own workflow builder.

pricingBreakdown: Chatbase's pricing is a straight message-credit ladder, not a seat count: 50 credits free, 700 for $40/mo on Hobby, 4,000 for $150/mo on Standard, 15,000 for $500/mo on Pro (roughly 20% cheaper — $32/$120/$400 — if you commit to annual billing) — but that sticker price only tells half the story until you know which model you're pointing at, since a premium model can burn 5 credits on a single reply while a lighter model burns 1. That makes real cost-per-conversation genuinely unpredictable from the pricing page alone, a different failure mode than Wonderchat's resolution-based billing (you pay per successfully-handled conversation, not per model call) or Tidio's Lyro add-on, which starts at $32.50/mo for just 50 AI conversations — a much smaller bucket than Chatbase's Hobby tier buys, but at least it's a number you can actually plan around. The $150/mo Standard tier is the one that matters if you want more than a toy bot, since it's the first tier with voice, telephony, and helpdesk features — that puts it above Crisp's Essentials plan ($95/mo), and Crisp's $95/mo buys a real omnichannel shared inbox across WhatsApp, Instagram, and email, not a website bot with a ticketing veneer bolted on top.

capabilities.note: This is the entire product — you crawl a site or upload documents, tune a prompt, and the bot answers from that content. It's genuinely fast to get live, but the credit-metering model means the AI's cost and its quality are tied to the same dial: pick a cheaper model to save credits and you're more likely to run into the hallucination complaints that show up repeatedly in independent reviews.

Training sources cover crawled pages, uploaded documents, plain text, and Q&A pairs, with auto-retraining from Standard tier up. The catch worth internalizing: a crawl is a snapshot, not a live feed, so anything that changes often (prices, stock, policies) needs a manual recrawl or an API integration rather than being trusted to update itself.

Outbound campaign tooling shows up on the Standard plan and above, letting the bot proactively message rather than just wait for a question. It's a real feature, but it's bolted onto an AI-agent product rather than being a mature campaign-builder in its own right — don't expect ManyChat-level broadcast sophistication here.

A helpdesk/ticketing layer unlocks at Standard ($150/mo, or $120/mo billed annually), with ticket-sourcing analytics arriving at Pro. Treat this as a light layer for routing AI-escalated conversations to a human, not a full team-inbox replacement — if a shared inbox is the actual thing you need most, this isn't where Chatbase is strongest.

What ships is a website widget that fronts the AI agent, not a live-chat system built around humans typing back and forth in real time. Independent hands-on reviews specifically flag that Chatbase lacks the built-in live-chat/human-handoff experience that Crisp or Tidio ship by default — the AI is meant to be the front line here, with humans as a fallback, not the other way around.

pros: Very fast to get a working bot live from an existing website with no coding required
Flexible knowledge sources (crawl, documents, text, Q&A) cover most small-to-mid business content needs
Bootstrapped, founder-led company with reportedly strong revenue growth, suggesting product-market fit and staying power
Higher tiers add real depth — voice, telephony, ticketing, and business-system integrations, not just a wider widget
cons: Credit-based pricing makes monthly costs hard to predict, especially once premium models are involved
Multiple independent reviews report hallucinated or made-up answers outside the trained content
Add-ons (extra agents, custom domain, branding removal) meaningfully raise the effective price beyond the sticker plan cost
Customer support quality lags behind product ease-of-use according to third-party review aggregates

sentiment.quote: Easy to use & get set up without building from scratch
Terrible. I was lied to about if this product was supported
sentiment.source: Capterra review title (Jon A., Customer Success Manager, Financial Services)

bestFor: Solo founders and small teams who want a fast, no-code website support bot
Businesses with well-documented static content (FAQs, policies, guides) suited to crawl-based training
Teams wanting to bolt on voice/telephony or ticketing later without switching platforms
Budget-conscious buyers who can keep message volume within a predictable credit range
verdict: Chatbase earns its popularity on pure setup speed, and pointing it at a website and having a working bot live in minutes is genuinely as easy as it sounds. A solo founder bootstrapping to a reported $9M ARR without outside money says something real about retention, because nobody keeps paying month after month for a bot that quietly embarrasses their brand. What you actually need to watch is the credit-metering model: burning 5 credits per reply on a premium model versus 1 on a lighter model means two businesses sitting on the identical $150/mo Standard plan can end up with wildly different real costs per conversation, and that's not a hypothetical edge case — it's just how the pricing page works (and note the sticker prices are the monthly rate; committing to annual billing knocks about 20% off). Support quality consistently trails ease-of-use in third-party reviews, so budget for the support experience matching the weaker signal, not the flashier one. Use it as a fast-to-launch FAQ bot and it'll do exactly what you're paying for; try to make it your full customer-support system of record and you'll start missing what Intercom or Zendesk do with a real shared inbox underneath the AI.
